Belgium

30 ads · €11216 spend · 239 purchases
✅ What's Working
• #2 variants crush #1 variants in every concept pair—Summer, Split, Catalog, iMessage, Heart Tag—showing second iterations always win.
• The lone Carousel (Carousel_120237873305580396 - Copy) is the best performer at 4.04x ROAS and €25.05 CPP but only got €426 in spend—massively starved.
• "Static _ Summer #2" is the volume engine: 70 purchases, €28.63 CPP, 3.31x ROAS—carrying the account on its back.
❌ What's Not Working
• Solitaire concept is a black hole: €2,109 combined spend across both variants with blended 1.14x ROAS—"Static _ Solitaire #1" alone burned €1,937 at 1.27x.
• Heart creatives generate vanity CTRs (181–221%) but fail to convert—"Static _ Heart Tag #1" (0.83x), "Static _ Heart White #1" (0.69x), and "Static _ Heart Split #1" (0.99x) are click traps.
• Wrong Tennis execution got the budget: "Static _ Tennis #6" ate €394 at 0.91x while Tennis #2 (6.36x) and Tennis #5 (5.89x) were starved on pennies.
⬆ Double Down On
• Carousel format everywhere—only one exists and it's the #1 ROAS ad; produce carousel variants of Summer, Heart, and iMessage concepts immediately.
• Video ads: "Video _ General #3" at 3.59x ROAS is the only video in the mix—massive untapped format gap, create product-specific and UGC videos.
• iMessage concept iteration: #2 variant hits 2.97x ROAS with strong CTR—test in motion, carousel, and UGC formats to find the ceiling.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Solitaire concept entirely—both variants are underwater, €2,109 wasted with zero sign of improvement.
• Every #1 variant that has a winning #2 sibling (Split #1, Heart Tag #1, iMessage #1, Catalog #1)—stop splitting budget with proven losers.
• All high-CTR / low-ROAS Heart statics (Heart White #1, Heart Split #1)—vanity clicks are not revenue.

Kamping Kitsch Club — Ads Report

14 September 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €1251 spend · 1009 purchases
✅ What's Working
• "Last Call" urgency messaging dominates — 6 variants averaging 65x ROAS with CPPs under €1.10, led by "Video _ Last Call #1 - Copy" at 113x ROAS and "Static _ Last Call #1 - Copy" driving 121 purchases at €0.62 CPP.
• Static creative is quietly crushing video — 17 of 20 ads are statics producing 95%+ of purchase volume at lower production cost, directly contradicting the video-first strategy assumption.
• Flemish-dialect and artist-name hooks ("Waar vo", "RUBEN", "Hart #2") drive sub-€1.25 CPPs — cultural specificity and name recognition convert hard in this market.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Video _ Aftermovie #1" is the worst performer by a mile — €7.79 CPP, 3 purchases, 11x ROAS. Brand vibes don't sell tickets in conversion campaigns.
• Generic informational ads bleed opportunity cost — "Static _ Update #1" (€3.07 CPP) and "Static _ Weather #1" (€4.24 CPP) cost 4-7x more per purchase than urgency creatives.
• Repurposed organic content ("Organic #5" at €3.26 CPP, 8 purchases) wasn't built for conversion and performs accordingly — high CTR, weak purchase rate.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce 4-5 new urgency static variants — countdown timers, ticket scarcity warnings, price-increase deadlines. "Last Call" proves this angle has unlimited headroom at sub-€1 CPP.
• Build a repeatable artist-spotlight static template modeled on "RUBEN" (49.6x ROAS) and "Hart #2" (43.6x ROAS) — one per headliner, direct ticket CTA, Flemish copy.
• Shift creative production from video-first to static-first — statics are cheaper to produce, faster to iterate, and outperforming video on every conversion metric except the Last Call video variants.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running aftermovies as conversion creative — €7.79 CPP is 12x worse than your best ad. Relegate to awareness-only campaigns or organic.
• Stop producing vague "update" and "weather" hooks for paid — no urgency means no conversions. Every euro there could go to a Last Call variant instead.
• Stop boosting raw organic posts without reworking them for conversion — "Organic #5" proves reposts leak budget.

Belgium

30 ads · €6806 spend · 138 results
✅ What's Working
• Calculator/Berekening statics crush it — both #1 (€31.75 CPR) and #2 (€36.69 CPR, 23 leads) make savings tangible and drive action consistently.
• 'Static _ Smart #1 - Copy' is the runaway winner at €19.71 CPR with 7 leads on only €138 spend — whatever this creative does, it's the blueprint to reverse-engineer.
• Original 'General Video #1' (€742 spend) is the volume workhorse at €26.50 CPR with 28 leads — video storytelling converts when it's the original, not a copy.
❌ What's Not Working
• Every 'General Video #1 - Copy' variant is dead — €550+ combined spend across three copies, zero results despite absurd CTR (up to 1701%). Massive click-to-conversion disconnect signals broken targeting or landing page mismatch.
• Vergelijking #1 copies are wildly inconsistent: three entries range from €32.25 to €170.26 CPR. The concept is fragmented across audiences and burning cash on the wrong placements.
• Soft brand angles flop — 'De Tijd 2' (€109 CPR) and 'Dichtbij #1' (€122 CPR) prove that press credibility and proximity messaging don't drive direct-response action for Belgian sellers.
⬆ Double Down On
• Build more Berekening/calculator variants — test different home price anchors (€250K, €350K, €500K) to segment by seller profile and make the savings feel personal.
• Iterate aggressively on the 'Smart' format — at €19.71 CPR this is the most efficient creative in the account and has room to scale with fresh variants.
• Launch French-language versions of the top 3 performers (Smart, Berekening, General Video) — Wallonia and Brussels are likely under-penetrated with only NL creatives dominating spend.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill every 'General Video #1 - Copy' variant immediately — three duplicates, combined €550 spend, zero leads. High CTR with no conversions is a vanity trap.
• Kill 'Static _ De Tijd 2' and 'Static _ Dichtbij #1' — press authority and proximity angles are not converting in a lead-gen funnel, combined €340 for 3 leads at €113 avg CPR.
• Kill 'Static _ Vergelijking #1 - Copy' (€170 spend, €170.26 CPR) and 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy 2' (€117 spent, 0 results) — both are confirmed money pits.

Belgium

25 ads · €5368 spend · 74 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Static split formats are your engine: Vuelta Split #1 (€683, 17 purchases, 2.46x ROAS at €40 CPP) and Vuelta Split #2 (€353, 2.13x) prove side-by-side product presentation converts cyclists.
• Clean product-focused statics crush everything: Product Ziris #2 delivers 4.14x ROAS at a ridiculous €27.74 CPP, and Colors #1 hits 3.04x at €47.77 — simple product hero shots sell glasses.
• Statics outperform video at every level: the top 5 ROAS ads are all statics. Video is draining budget for mediocre returns.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video Sieben ads are a budget sinkhole: €1,479 combined spend across four Sieben variants, blended ROAS barely above 1.3x. Sieben Split #2 burned €222 for zero purchases.
• HelboF Before&After ads are a vanity metrics trap: 130-163% CTR but literally zero conversions across €166 spend — people click, nobody buys.
• Vuelta 'Full' formats consistently flop vs 'Split': both Vuelta Full #2 variants sit at 0.84x and 1.14x ROAS. The full-frame layout kills purchase intent.
⬆ Double Down On
• Replicate the Product Ziris #2 format (clean product hero static) across every product line — Helbo, Selva Snow, sunglasses. This 4.14x formula is begging to be scaled.
• Double down on static split/color-option layouts: Vuelta Split and Colors #1 prove that showing multiple colorways or lens options in one frame drives efficient purchases.
• Create prescription sports glasses ('op sterkte') specific creatives — your biggest differentiator vs Oakley and Decathlon is completely absent from the ad mix.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Sieben video variants — four ads, nearly €1.5K spent, combined ROAS around 1.3x. This concept is dead.
• Kill both HelboF Before&After creatives immediately. Zero conversions despite insane CTR means the creative promises something the landing page doesn't deliver.
• Kill both Vuelta Full formats — the 'Full' layout consistently underperforms 'Split' by 50%+ on ROAS. Stop testing what's already proven inferior.

🇧🇪

Belgium

15 ads · €2114 spend · 178 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Video exploration creatives are absurdly efficient — "Video _ XPL04 MG #1" (403x ROAS, €6.64 CPP) and "Video _ XPL04 KA #1" (189.63x ROAS, €2.44 CPP) are printing money at minimal spend, likely origin story content that resonates deeply with specialty coffee enthusiasts.
• Catalog carousel for espresso is the workhorse — "Catalog Carousel - Espresso Coffee" drives the most volume (48 purchases) at a healthy 22.93x ROAS, proving product-feed creative converts at scale.
• Static retention/hold creatives punch above their weight — "Static _ Hold #1" delivers 49.38x ROAS at just €216 spend, and "Static_Barista_Courses - Copy" hits 44.45x ROAS, suggesting existing customers and barista-curious audiences convert cheaply.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Static _ Origin #1" is the biggest miss — €83 spent, only 2 purchases, €41.32 CPP, 10.5x ROAS. For a brand built on origin stories, a static image isn't doing the narrative justice; this concept needs video.
• "Static _ Hold #2" is dead weight — €43 for 1 purchase, 5.47x ROAS, €43.23 CPP. Whatever variant this is versus Hold #1 (49.38x ROAS), it's clearly the loser.
• "Static _ General #1" spent €10 with zero purchases. Low spend but zero signal of life — generic messaging doesn't cut it in specialty coffee.
⬆ Double Down On
• Origin exploration videos (XPL format) — the XPL04 KA and MG variants are the best-performing creatives by ROAS. Produce more origin-specific video content for different beans/regions. This is the format that wins.
• Catalog carousels segmented by use case — espresso carousel works, now build versions for filter, subscription bundles, and seasonal picks to capture different intent.
• Barista culture + education angle — "Static_Barista_Courses - Copy" and "Static _ Barista #1" both convert efficiently. Lean into educational content: brew guides, course promos, barista tips as video and static.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill "Static _ Hold #2" immediately — it's the inferior variant and the data is clear after €43. Hold #1 wins, move on.
• Kill "Static _ General #1" — zero purchases, generic positioning. Specialty coffee buyers don't respond to 'general.' Every ad needs a specific hook.
• Kill "Static _ Origin #1" as a static — the origin story angle works in video (see XPL ads), not as a flat image. Retire this format and redirect budget to video origin content.

Creative Analysis

10 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

10 ads · €302 spend · 3 purchases
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ USvThem #1" is the only profitable concept in the account — 14.33x ROAS at a €32.62 CPP proves comparison messaging converts Belgian coffee buyers.
• CTRs are strong across nearly every creative (100%+ on most), meaning the visual hooks are grabbing attention — the bottleneck is post-click conversion, not interest.
• The Us-vs-Them differentiation angle clearly aligns with an audience that cares about quality over convenience — lean into this identity play.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Static _ Search #1" is a total flop — €53 combined spend across two instances, zero purchases, and the weakest CTR in the set (51.45%). The concept is dead.
• "Static _ Chat #1" spent €19 across two instances with zero conversions. Conversational framing isn't driving purchase intent for this audience.
• "Static _ Review #2" technically converted once but at 1.18x ROAS (€55.93 CPP) — that's losing money. Social proof alone isn't closing the sale without a stronger offer or differentiation hook.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more USvThem variations: cost-per-cup vs café, Mister Barish vs supermarket beans, specialty vs commodity — the comparison framework is the only proven converter.
• Create authority-driven content that leverages the "we test every machine on the market" USP — this is a unique differentiator no competitor can easily copy.
• Pair social proof with an offer or USP — reviews alone flopped, but reviews layered on top of a comparison or expertise angle could compound the winning formula.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill "Static _ Search #1" immediately — both instances are money pits with zero signal of life.
• Kill "Static _ Chat #1" — the conversational concept has no conversion signal and is eating budget that should go to USvThem scaling.
• Stop running identical creatives in different ad sets hoping for different results — the €92 USvThem instance with 0 purchases vs the €65 instance with 14.33x ROAS screams audience or placement mismatch, not creative problem.

Belgium

12 ads · €369 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Nothing is converting — zero results across all 12 ads and €368 total spend. The entire account is in emergency mode.
• Extremely high reported CTRs (100%+) across most ads suggest people ARE clicking, pointing to a post-click or tracking problem rather than pure creative failure.
• Three distinct creative angles (Myth, General, USvsTHEM) are being tested systematically — the framework is sound even if results are broken.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero conversions on €368 spend screams broken conversion tracking, misconfigured pixel, or a landing page that kills all intent. Fix this before spending another euro.
• All creatives are static — no video, no carousel, no UGC. For a considered €1,000+ purchase like EV charging installation, static alone won't educate or build enough trust to convert.
• Duplicate ad names running simultaneously (e.g., two 'Static _ Myth #1', two 'Static _ Myth #2') suggest messy ad set structure cannibalizing budget with no learnings gained.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the funnel first: audit pixel firing, thank-you page events, and landing page load speed in Belgium before any new creative spend.
• Develop video creative — installation walkthroughs, customer testimonials, before/after setups — to build trust for a high-consideration product.
• Localize for Belgium: test French-language variants (Wallonia) alongside Dutch (Flanders) — one language won't cover this market.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all duplicate ad variants immediately — consolidate budget into single instances per creative to give Meta's algorithm a chance to optimize.
• Stop running static-only creative for a high-ticket installation product — it's insufficient to drive conversions without social proof or demonstration.
• Stop spending until conversion tracking is verified end-to-end. Every euro spent now is waste.

Belgium

4 ads · €927 spend · 62 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 2" is the only ad with meaningful spend and delivers 62 leads at €14.84 — strong cost/lead for real estate, proving the investment angle resonates with Belgian audiences.
• Static format paired with an investment hook clearly earns algorithmic trust — Meta consolidated nearly all budget here, signaling strong engagement signals.
• The "Investeren" framing taps into a rational buyer mindset (100% rental guarantee, returns) that converts at scale in this market.
❌ What's Not Working
• Creative diversity is essentially zero — four static investment variants with near-identical naming, giving Meta's algorithm nothing meaningfully different to test across audiences.
• "Static _ Investeren" flatlined at 0.00% CTR and zero results — the original variant is dead creative that should have been killed days ago.
• Three of four ads barely cleared €4 in spend, meaning the campaign is running on a single creative leg — one fatigue cycle away from total collapse.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more investment-angle statics with fresh visual treatments — the hook works, but you need 4-5 variations ready to rotate before "Static _ Investeren _ 2" fatigues.
• Launch lifestyle and emotional creative (water, panoramic views, rust en ruimte) to open an entirely untapped messaging lane targeting second-home and primary-residence buyers.
• Create video and motion formats — zero video exists in this account; a kijkwoning walkthrough or drone flyover of the Westerschelde could dramatically expand reach and lower CPLs.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running all four ads as near-identical static investment variants — this is a testing failure, not a testing strategy.
• Kill "Static _ Investeren" immediately — 0% CTR, zero results, wasting even pennies is an insult to the pixel.

Other

17 ads · €4539 spend · 288 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Water Wind _ Form" is the undisputed champion — 115 leads at €8.06 CPR, nearly 3x more volume than any other ad. Emotional lifestyle hook + embedded form is the winning formula.
• Product-specific apartment ads convert efficiently: "Static _ Nieuw_App #1" delivers the lowest CPR at €7.78 and "Static _ Video #2" hits €9.94 — concrete product angles paired with low friction work.
• Visit-oriented CTAs still pull: "Static _ Visit #2 - Copy" earns 36 leads at €9.81, proving kijkwoning visit framing resonates with this audience.
❌ What's Not Working
• Social proof falls flat: "Static _ Review _ Form" burns €796 for just 20 leads at €39.80 CPR — nearly 5x worse than top performer. Testimonials aren't moving the needle for prospect-stage audiences.
• "Dreamer" creatives are all romance, no conversion: "Static _ Dreamer #1" (€23.97 CPR) and "Static _ Dreamer #2" (€31.49 CPR) have sky-high CTRs but attract dreamers not buyers. Beautiful but inefficient.
• "Static _ Opsomming #2" soaks up the most budget (€1076) yet delivers a bloated €29.09 CPR — bullet-point feature dumps don't convert at scale compared to emotional or product-focused hooks.
⬆ Double Down On
• Lifestyle-meets-form statics: replicate the "Water Wind" formula — evocative waterfront imagery, short emotive copy, instant lead form. Produce 2-3 new variants with different Westerschelde visuals and seasonal angles.
• Apartment-specific product ads: "Nieuw_App" proves that concrete product framing (new apartments, pricing signals, turnkey messaging) converts cheaply. Create variants for houses and hotel apartments with investment angle.
• Short video with product focus: "Video #2" quietly delivers at €9.94 CPR on modest spend. Scale video production — walkthrough kijkwoning clips, drone Westerschelde footage, 15-second lifestyle reels with clear CTA.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause "Static _ Review _ Form" immediately — €39.80 CPR is unacceptable when you have ads running at €8. Social proof isn't earning its keep.
• Kill "Static _ Visit #1" — €62 spent, zero leads, dead on arrival. The #2 copy version works; this one doesn't.
• Stop scaling "Static _ Opsomming #2" — at €1076 it's your biggest spender but 3.6x more expensive per lead than "Water Wind." Feature lists aren't the move.

❌ What's Not Working

• The entire account is 100% static creative — zero video, zero Reels. You're ignoring Meta's highest-reach format and leaving the 18–35 demo underserved.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more B2B occasion variants: expand the winning framework (brunch, boost, 4 moments) into summer menus, healthy kids' options, post-workout recovery — the template is proven, iterate on it.
• Launch video and Reels creative immediately — static-only is a strategic blind spot; test short-form bowl prep, behind-the-scenes sourcing, and endorser content to unlock new reach.
• Build a proper B2C retail-driving campaign with explicit "Find us at Bio-Planet & Delhaize" CTAs, leveraging Bekkari/Binge/Gruyaert — the current B2C efforts have no purchase pathway.
🛑 Kill or Rethink

• Kill "Static _ Bowl #1" — €126 spent with zero results is inexcusable; the creative or funnel is fundamentally broken.

Other

9 ads · €494 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Nothing is working — zero results and zero ROAS across all 9 ads, totaling ~€492 burned.
• Sky-high CTR numbers (344–696%) suggest these are boosted Instagram posts generating engagement clicks (likes, comments), not purchase-intent traffic.
• "Evenement: Early bird start of the season days!" and "Instagram post: New!! Delivery winter 2026" show the highest CTRs, hinting urgency/newness hooks generate curiosity — but none of it converts.
❌ What's Not Working
• Every single ad has 0 tracked results — this is a systemic tracking or campaign-objective failure, not a creative problem. Pixel/CAPI is likely broken or campaigns are set to Engagement instead of Conversions/Sales.
• Boosted posts dominate the account ("Instagram-bericht" variants). These are the worst-performing ad format for driving purchases.
• Mixed Dutch/English copy with no clear CTA or product focus (e.g., "Instagram-bericht: ❤️" is literally just an emoji) — zero commercial intent in the creative.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the foundation FIRST: install Meta Pixel + Conversions API, set campaigns to Purchase objective, and build proper Ads Manager campaigns — not boosted posts.
• Lean into urgency and newness hooks — "Early bird," "New deliveries," and seasonal drops generated the highest engagement; rebuild these as conversion-optimized ads with clear product shots and CTAs.
• Create product-hero creatives with pricing, single-product focus, and direct shop-now CTAs — the current posts are brand-diary content, not performance ads.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting Instagram posts immediately — every euro spent this way is unmeasurable vanity spend.
• Kill all ads with no clear product, price, or CTA — "Instagram-bericht: ❤️" and generic "Instagram-bericht" variants are content, not ads.

🇧🇪

Belgium

2 ads · €90 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Both ads (120239393986810631, 120239394435940631) are generating abnormally high CTRs (124%+ and 101%+), indicating the creative hooks are grabbing attention and driving clicks — people in Belgium clearly respond to workwear messaging.
• Low spend levels (€50 and €39) mean damage is contained while testing, which is smart for early-stage campaigns.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero conversions across both ads despite high click volume — this screams broken conversion tracking, a misaligned landing page, or a fundamentally broken funnel. The ads are doing their job; everything after the click is failing.
• Neither ad (120239393986810631, 120239394435940631) has produced a single measurable result, meaning all €89 spent is pure waste until the downstream funnel is fixed.
• CTRs above 100% are a red flag — likely measuring all clicks (including multiple per user) rather than unique outbound clicks, which may mean engagement is inflated by curiosity clicks, not purchase intent.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix conversion tracking and landing page BEFORE spending another euro — the click-through demand clearly exists, but the funnel is leaking 100% of traffic.
• Once tracking is fixed, lean into the high-CTR creative style already proven in both ads — the hooks are working for this Belgian B2B audience.
• Develop workwear-specific social proof content (client logos, team photos in branded gear, before/after uniform rollouts) to bridge the gap between ad click and conversion.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop all ad spend immediately until conversion tracking is verified end-to-end — pixel, events, thank-you page, the works. Every euro right now is untrackable waste.
• Kill any assumption that high CTR equals success — without conversions, clicks are just expensive window shopping.

✅ What's Working
• 'Video _ Call #2 - Copy' is the only ad with multiple purchases (2) at €45 CPP — proof-of-concept that real interaction footage converts.
• 'Video _ DM #2 - Copy' and 'Static _ Matthias #1' each drove 1 purchase — personal, authentic formats outperform polished business messaging.
• Video ads showing real conversations (calls, DMs) generate all 4 purchases despite receiving under 6% of total spend.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Static _ Business #1 - Copy' and 'Static _ Business #1' burned €2,391 combined with zero purchases — generic business messaging is a cash incinerator.
• All 6 Concierge video variants (€591 total) produced zero purchases and have the lowest relative CTRs — the concept is dead.
• 'Static _ Review #1 - Copy', 'Static _ Rip #1', and 'Video _ Talking Head' variants spent €1,082 combined with zero purchases — social proof and talking head formats aren't landing.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more 'Call' format videos showing live client conversations — only format with multiple purchases and best CPP by far.
• Create more personal/founder content featuring Matthias or named team members — personalization drives the only static purchase.
• Invest in DM-style conversation videos — 'Video _ DM #2 - Copy' converted at 1 purchase and the format feels native to Meta feeds.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all 'Business' static variants immediately — €2,454 burned across 4 ads with zero results.
• Kill the entire Concierge video series — 6 placements, €591 wasted, zero signal of life.
• Stop running Talking Head videos — €382 spent on two variants with nothing to show.

✅ What's Working
• Vottem project dominates efficiency: Vottem_apt (€20/result), Vottem_video (€28), Vottem_animatie (€29) — animation and video formats crush static for this project.
• Brugge_penthouse is the volume king: 25 results at €37.47 with the highest spend — proven scalable creative.
• Video and animation formats consistently outperform: west_video (€41, 12 results) vs west_ext (€76, 9 results); Vottem_animatie (€29) vs Vottem_logements (€44) — motion wins.
❌ What's Not Working
• Reels format is a money pit: wildebeek_reel (€206/result), Awans_reel (€208/result) — burning cash with almost zero conversions.
• Charleroi is bleeding: Charleroi_native (€183/result), Charleroi_te-huur (€200/result) — both formats failing badly, likely audience or offer problem.
• georges_slideshow spent €258 for literally zero results — dead on arrival. Georges ads overall are mediocre at best (€63-74/result).
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Vottem creative variants: this project converts at 2-4x efficiency of everything else — test new angles, walkthroughs, lifestyle hooks.
• Scale video/animation formats across ALL projects: the pattern is clear — motion content delivers 40-60% lower CPR than static/image ads.
• Replicate Brugge_penthouse approach for other premium units: high-aspiration property creative with strong CTR and volume — apply this template to Stokerie, Blom, Georges.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all reel-format ads immediately — wildebeek_reel and Awans_reel are €200+ per result with negligible volume.
• Kill georges_slideshow — €258 spent, zero results, no signal worth saving.
• Kill or completely rethink Charleroi — both ads are above €180/result; current creative and/or targeting is fundamentally broken.

30 ads · €4060 spend · 154 results
✅ What's Working
• Doorstromer 'Copy' variants are the clear winners — #2 Copy at €9.53/result and #1 Copy at €13.22/result with 88 conversions dominate the account.
• Original creative versions consistently crush V2 reworks — every V2 variant has worse CPR or zero results, proving the original direction was right.
• Jong Koppel #1 quietly delivered €6.97/result (best CPR in the account) on just €21 spend — a hidden gem starved of budget.
❌ What's Not Working
• V2 creatives are a disaster across the board — Doorstromer V2 #1 burned €723 at €103/result (8x worse than the original Copy), General V2 #1 wasted €278 at €93/result, Algemeen #2 V2 spent €181 for 1 lonely result.
• Alleenstaand audience is underperforming — #2 has volume at €24.38 but #1, #1 V2, and #2 V2 combined spent €174 for zero results.
• ODD ads (#4, #5) have sky-high CTR but negligible conversions — high curiosity clicks that don't convert.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Doorstromer creatives using the original (non-V2) visual style and messaging — this audience and creative direction is carrying the entire account.
• Scale Jong Koppel aggressively — €6.97 CPR signals strong product-market fit for young couples, just needs budget to validate at scale.
• Create variations of the #2 Copy treatment specifically — it has the best CPR in the account and is barely funded at €86.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill every V2 creative immediately — they represent a collective €1,354 in spend with drastically worse performance than originals. The redesign failed.
• Kill ODD ads — high CTR masking zero meaningful conversion. Clickbait without payoff.
• Stop splitting budget across 20 ads — consolidate into 5-6 proven performers to exit learning phase faster.

🌐

Other

3 ads · €169 spend · 1 results
✅ What's Working
• PERGOLAS ad is the only one generating any result at all — pergolas as a product hook has some traction.
• Absurdly high CTRs across all three ads (130-200%) suggest creative is grabbing attention and generating engagement, even if conversions are absent.
• Product-specific ad naming (PERGOLAS vs PVC VER vs VERANDAS) shows good segmentation instinct — right structure, wrong execution.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero ROAS across the board — not a single ad is provably profitable. Total spend €170 for 1 result at €134.52 is brutal.
• PVC. VER.- PUB CONVERTION and VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS both spent budget with zero results — clicks without conversions signals a broken funnel or weak offer.
• Massive CTR-to-conversion gap everywhere suggests the post-click experience (landing page, form, CTA) is leaking leads, not the ads themselves.
⬆ Double Down On
• Pergola-specific creative — only product that converted. Build a full creative suite around this product line.
• High-intent lead magnets (free on-site quote, 3D design preview) to fix the conversion gap between click and result.
• Localized social proof — show completed installations in the specific region to build trust and shorten the decision cycle.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Generic multi-product ads with no clear CTA or offer — the current creative is curiosity bait with no conversion mechanism.
• Running conversion campaigns on budgets under €10/day — €7 and €28 total spend gives Meta zero data to optimize. Either commit €15+/day per ad set or don't run it.

• Same creative in multiple ad sets produces wildly inconsistent results — 'PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_MUTLI4' ranges from €16.49 to €147.87 CPR, meaning budget is bleeding into losing placements without proper exclusions.

• Static single-image format for conversion-focused ads — it beat carousel and gif on the only metric that matters (results).
• Location-specific creatives featuring Duinpanne-style nature destinations — the location outperformed Gavers and Zwin, test more like it.

• Pause "IZWVL - Janneke - Gavers" immediately — €114 per result is indefensible for a provincial government campaign.

✅ What's Working
• Reel format is the only format converting — 'Post
• Reel Mary-Lynn' delivered 3.5x ROAS and €11.42 CPP on tiny spend, proving product-on-body video sells.
• Low-spend Reels ('Merlene', 'Marie Jo Lisbeth') show strong CTR signals suggesting the format resonates even before conversion data matures.
❌ What's Not Working
• Boosted 'Bericht' posts are a money pit — €452 spent across six static/text posts with exactly zero purchases. These are engagement bait, not sales drivers.
• Event promotions ('Feestelijke opening', 'XXL STOCK SALE!') spent €70 combined with zero conversions — likely running awareness/engagement objectives, not purchase-optimized campaigns.
• Absurd CTRs (300-999%) across the board confirm these are boosted posts counting reactions/shares as clicks — vanity metrics masking zero commercial return.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product-focused Reels showing specific lingerie pieces on a model (like Mary-Lynn) — this is your only proven conversion format. Produce at scale.
• Conversion-optimized campaign structure: stop boosting posts, build proper Sales/Purchase objective campaigns with dedicated landing pages.
• Hero product spotlights for premium brands (PrimaDonna, Marie Jo) in short-form video — the product interest is there, the ad format and objective are wrong.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All boosted organic posts immediately — they are not set up to track or drive purchases.
• Generic store announcements and event promotions as paid ads — use organic reach for awareness, reserve paid budget exclusively for conversion-optimized product ads.
